method: Brewing salts add ions by mass, so the arithmetic is stoichiometric. The mole fraction of each ion in a salt's formula mass turns a weighed dose into milligrams per litre: ppm = 1000 x grams x (ion mass / salt molar mass) / litres, with ion masses Ca 40.078, Mg 24.305, Na 22.9898, Cl 35.45, SO4 96.056 and HCO3 61.0168 built from IUPAC standard atomic weights. The salts are the hydrates brewing suppliers sell: gypsum CaSO4.2H2O (172.164 g/mol) gives 61.5 ppm calcium and 147.4 ppm sulfate per gram per US gallon, calcium chloride dihydrate CaCl2.2H2O (147.008) gives 72.0 ppm calcium and 127.4 ppm chloride, Epsom salt MgSO4.7H2O (246.466) gives 26.1 ppm magnesium and 103.0 ppm sulfate, table salt NaCl (58.440) gives 103.9 ppm sodium and 160.3 ppm chloride, and baking soda NaHCO3 (84.006) gives 72.3 ppm sodium and 191.9 ppm bicarbonate. The first three sit inside the ranges Brew Your Own publishes; table salt and baking soda follow the same formula. Anhydrous calcium chloride would give 95 ppm calcium from the same weight, so the page names the hydrate form. Starting-water concentrations are added to the contributions before any rounding. Total hardness and alkalinity are reported as calcium carbonate equivalents through the 50.043 g/eq half-mole of CaCO3: hardness = calcium x 50.043 / 20.039 + magnesium x 50.043 / 12.153, alkalinity = bicarbonate x 50.043 / 61.017. The sulfate to chloride ratio comes from the exact concentrations, is shown to two decimals, and is suppressed as no chloride when none is present. ppm is milligrams per litre, so a US gallon is 3.785411784 L. Volume runs from 0.1 to 10,000 litres or 0.1 to 2,600 US gallons, each salt from 0 to 1,000 grams and each starting concentration from 0 to 2,000 ppm, all with at most three decimals and no sign or exponent notation; a malformed or out-of-range value is refused with a field-specific message. The page reports ion concentrations only: it does not model mash pH or acid additions, and chalk is not offered because it dissolves poorly. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
